bioAdditions:
North Carolina State's football programmes from the Lou Holtz years confirm Danny's college career and tie him to Levittown. The 1974 roster lists "*Dan Meier", middle guard, 234 lb, of Levittown, Pa., where the asterisk marks one varsity letter already won. The 1975 roster lists "**Dan Meier, Levittown, Pa." with two letters. The 1976 outlook names "tackle Dan Meier" among the chief losses from the 1975 team (S1, S2, S3). He therefore lettered in 1973, 1974 and 1975, playing middle guard and tackle.

After retiring as Robinson principal he kept stepping in as a stand-in principal. He was interim principal of Herndon High in autumn 2016, where he had once been director of counselling (S4), and of Oakton High in spring 2017. There he told the student paper that he had been a football coach for 17 years, a history teacher, guidance counsellor, director of student services, assistant principal and principal of Rocky Run and Robinson, and that he had filled in at Herndon, Woodson, Madison and four or five middle schools (S5). His sons' West Point athletic biographies call their parents "Dan and Ann Meier" and note that their father played football, as a defensive lineman, at North Carolina State (S7, S8).
funFacts: His sons Mike and Tim later shared the Army sprint football backfield; in 2010 Mike led Army in rushing (48.8 yards a game) with Tim second (48.5).
openQuestionsNew: Four Washington Post archive stories found by search but not loadable (403): 17 Dec 1989 "West Potomac's trickery brings state title, 17-14"; 1 Sep 1989 "For West Potomac, pride is growing"; 5 Sep 1986 "West Potomac will be no surprise"; 8 Dec 1996 "No. 1 Chantilly 14, GW-Danville 7". See leads.
NC State University Libraries' photograph collection (UA023) has individual portraits of 1973-75 players; a portrait of Dan Meier may exist but d.lib.ncsu.edu was blocked (bot challenge, HTTP 401).
High school in Levittown not identified. No Meier appears in Ted Silary's Bishop Egan football history or the Conwell-Egan Sports Hall of Fame list.
